summary: The old harness cannot recursively unpack a nested object or array on either source version.

claims.necessity_reason: Nested object and array formats are supported within the harness’s json_unpack operation. A valid nested JSON value can reach that operation, but every fixed member or element format uses generic o, which returns the value without unpacking its contents.

before.requirement: Use a nested object or array format to unpack a structure contained in an input value.
before.reason: The before source dispatches nested formats recursively. The harness supplies only o for object members and array elements; o extracts a pointer without recursive unpacking.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: An object member is passed to unpack using its member format.
An array element is passed to unpack using its element format.
Generic o assigns the value to an output pointer without descending into it.

after.requirement: Use a nested object or array format to unpack a structure contained in an input value.
after.reason: Recursive dispatch remains available. The same fixed harness formats still select o for members and elements, so nested structures are returned without recursive unpacking.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: An object member is passed to unpack using its member format.
An array element is passed to unpack using its element format.
Generic o assigns the value to an output pointer without descending into it.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The fuzzer supplies JSON bytes that are parsed before unpacking.

claims.comparison_reason: Both versions support nested-format dispatch, and the same old harness lacks a nested member or element format on both sides.
